subject: chemistry-1
question: Which example is best classified as an ionic compound, and how many ions are present in one of its formula units?

options.text: MgCl2, which contains 3 ions per formula unit
CO2, which contains 3 ions per formula unit
CH4, which contains 5 ions per formula unit
N2, which contains 2 ions per formula unit

explanation:
Ionic compounds typically form between a metal and a nonmetal; MgCl2 consists of one Mg2+ cation and two Cl- anions, giving 1 + 2 = 3 ions per formula unit. CH4, CO2, and N2 are molecular substances built entirely from nonmetal atoms joined by shared electron pairs, so they contain no ions at all, and counting their atoms is not the same as counting ions. Screening a formula for metal-plus-nonmetal composition is the fastest first test for ionic character.

ELI-10: Use a two-step sort. First, look for a metal paired with a nonmetal: magnesium is a metal and chlorine is not, so MgCl2 is ionic, while carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen are all nonmetals, making the other three molecular. Second, count charged pieces, not atoms. MgCl2 breaks into one Mg2+ and two Cl-, which is three ions. CH4 has five atoms but zero ions, which is the trap in that option.
source: OpenStax — Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e); NIST — Reference Data / Constants (https://www.nist.gov/pml)
